subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: plugin-emitted detectors and evals

question: Should external plugins be allowed to emit canonical AI-safety events, and what manifest authorization, provenance, privacy, and schema-version guarantees must the permanent Plugin SDK contract enforce?
rationale: This creates a durable public API and telemetry trust boundary; code review can assess an implementation, but it cannot choose OpenClaw's permanent spoofing, privacy, compatibility, and governance policy.

options.title: Approve a narrow gated API
options.body: Add one typed API after the core schema is approved, require declared event families for external plugins, validate bounded payloads, and preserve untrusted emitter provenance.

options.title: Restrict canonical events
options.body: Permit canonical safety events only from trusted core or bundled code and leave external detectors to plugin-owned telemetry until a stronger isolation model exists.

options.title: Defer the public taxonomy
options.body: Pause this API until the umbrella observability design demonstrates stable operator use cases and acceptable privacy and cardinality rules.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow gated API
recommendation.body: Add one typed API after the core schema is approved, require declared event families for external plugins, validate bounded payloads, and preserve untrusted emitter provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the affected Plugin SDK service-context boundary makes steipete the strongest available owner for routing the public API decision.
